{"inkVersion":21,"root":[["
",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^I am Bo Lindqvist. I drive a Granary truck on the Bowl road patrol. Sit down if you like. Most people who sit here have come to hear about a fight on the road, and I'll tell it once, if you want it.","
",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^What fight on the road?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^What is the road patrol?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^Do you call yourself a killer?","/str",{"VAR?":"bo_fight"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":5},"ev","str","^Why did you sign the patrol roll?","/str",{"VAR?":"bo_roll"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":5},"ev","str","^What is a Brann swivel?","/str",{"VAR?":"bo_fight"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^Where is Jens buried?","/str",{"VAR?":"bo_fight"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^What became of Jens's brother?","/str",{"VAR?":"bo_fight"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-7","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^The Vosk brothers had been stopping trucks on the Nose road for a long while. They always seemed to know which ones to stop. We carried a Brann swivel, a gun ring that swings across the truck bed, and I had never fired at a man.","
","^They came out of the wreck rows near the Burnt Convoy, the field of burned trucks beside the road. I swung the ring and I fired, and Jens went down in the road. I stopped the truck and went back to him, but he was already gone.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"bo_fight","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^I drive with it, and I count my years on its roll the way some men count debts. The roll is the list of drivers who guard the roads near Bowl. A tenant like me has no vote until he's served on it for a decade, so I've still got years to go.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"bo_roll","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^I do, whatever the hall says. The tenant hall, where the tenants meet, sat on it and decided that a tenant who defends his load isn't a killer. They were kind about it.","
","^I sat quiet while they said it. The hall can say what it likes, but I know what my hand did.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^For the vote, mostly, but I'd be lying if I said it was only that. A man on the road with a rifle should be a man who's thought about it. I've thought about it every night since that day.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^It's a ring of hull plate that swings across the truck bed and locks with a pin. I think about ours most nights. Otto Brann of Ridge Wrecks made it, and after that day he came and put a second pin on every swivel he'd made. He didn't say why, and he didn't need to.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^Brother Anselm, who buried the dead of that road, put him in the ground by Canyon Bridge. It's across the road from Hal Sorensen, who died of the same trouble years before. Anselm lies there too now, between them.","
","^Lusa Fenwick reads their names at the bridge once a year. I go, and I stay for all of it.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^He was never caught. Some say he hid among the squatters at the Burnt Convoy, and some say he rides for the raiders at Kiln Camp. I don't ask.","
","^If he came to my truck I'd give him the grain, and I'd give him water. I'd give him anything that bought Jens his life back.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","end",null]}],null]}],"global decl":["ev","str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"depot_thief"},false,{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen"},"str","^off","/str",{"VAR=":"intro_step"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pipe_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"sack_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"lamps_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"count_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"courier_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"names_vosk"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"hooks_report"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_fate"},"str","^hidden","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_pact"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"bend_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"crates_fate"},false,{"VAR=":"bo_fight"},false,{"VAR=":"bo_roll"},"/ev","end",null]}],"listDefs":{}}

bowl_dag.story:
{"inkVersion":21,"root":[["
",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^Dag. I ride with the Bowl Farmers, the patrol that keeps the roads near these walls. Keep your guns cold inside the gate and we'll get along fine.","
",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^What is the road like?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Any work?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^Who pays the Farmers?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":4},"ev","str","^Who are the raiders?","/str",{"VAR?":"dag_road"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":5},"ev","str","^What do you make of Nose?","/str",{"VAR?":"dag_road"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^What do you mean, pay the raiders?","/str",{"VAR?":"dag_kiln"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^Do tenants serve with you?","/str",{"VAR?":"dag_pay"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-7","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^Dusty, and worse every season. A truck that breaks down out there waits a long time for a friendly face, so carry water and a spare belt, and don't wander off the track.","
","^Raiders sniff around the roads too. It's nothing we can't run off, but you'll want your gun ready.","
","^The Army at Nose watches the stretch in front of its own gate, and it does that well enough.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"dag_road","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
",["ev",{"x()":"board_full"},"/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["
","^You're carrying enough promises already. Finish a few and then ask me again.","
",{"->":"start.hub"},{"->":".^.^.^.4"},null]}],["ev",{"x()":"has_work"},"!",{"x()":"has_offers"},"&&","/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["
","^There's nothing on the board you could take right now. Make some room on your truck and ask again.","
",{"->":"start.hub"},{"->":".^.^.^.4"},null]}],["ev",{"x()":"has_work"},"!","/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["
","^The board's empty today. Come back in a couple of days, it fills slowly.","
",{"->":"start.hub"},{"->":".^.^.^.4"},null]}],"nop","
","^I might have a haul for you, if you want it. ","#","^work_offer","/#","
",["ev","str","^I will take it.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Not now.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","ev",{"x()":"take_work"},"pop","/ev","
","^Good. Bowl remembers the people who deliver, so don't make me regret this.","
",{"->":"start.hub"},null],"c-1":["
",{"->":"start.hub"},null]}],null],"c-2":["
","^Not enough people, to be plain. The Granary pays out of its count of sacks. The drivers who cross Canyon Bridge pay a toll, the long convoys pay a fee, and the tenants put in a share of their harvest.","
","^Nose pays nothing, because it guards only its own walls. So each town watches the road by its own gate and nobody watches between the towns. I don't like it, and I don't know a cure.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"dag_pay","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^There's a pair of camps. Kiln Camp sits out east, south of the big crater, and Scrapjaw Camp is far up north. Most days they'd rather rob you than kill you, because a dead driver hauls nothing next week.","
","^So pay them or outrun them, but don't fire the first shot if you want to grow old.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"dag_kiln","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^The Army's all right on the road. Off it, they act as though the basin belongs to them and the rest of us are only borrowing it. Bowl was feeding people long before Nose put up its first fence.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^The Granary pays Kiln Camp a sack of grain for every armed truck that crosses their road. It costs less than a funeral.","
","^If they close on you anyway, fight hard. They often let a hard fighter go, and they strip a soft one down to the frame. Don't start the fight. But once they start it, don't hold back.","
","ev","str","^talkKilnFight","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^Some do. They're good drivers, but they've got no vote, so they ride in our coats without being on the roll of citizens. The Senate wants them on the road and off the roll.","
","^Jory Baptiste keeps sending more of them, and I can't decide whether to thank him or watch him.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","end",null]}],null]}],"global decl":["ev","str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"depot_thief"},false,{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen"},"str","^off","/str",{"VAR=":"intro_step"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pipe_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"sack_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"lamps_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"count_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"courier_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"names_vosk"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"hooks_report"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_fate"},"str","^hidden","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_pact"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"bend_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"crates_fate"},false,{"VAR=":"dag_road"},false,{"VAR=":"dag_kiln"},false,{"VAR=":"dag_pay"},"/ev","end",null]}],"listDefs":{}}

{"inkVersion":21,"root":[["
",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^Water's for paying folk, but talk's free. I'm Hattie, I keep the well house, and I hear everything that happens in Bowl twice. Once when it happens, and once when somebody's improved it. Bucket down and ears open.","
",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^Heard any rumors?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Any local legends?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^Who comes through here?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":4},"ev","str","^What do you make of the soldiers from Nose?","/str",{"VAR?":"hattie_strangers"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":5},"ev","str","^What about the glass at the Glass Flats?","/str",{"VAR?":"hattie_flats"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^Is it true the Sunward take strangers?","/str",{"VAR?":"hattie_sunward"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^Funny you ask. A scavenger came through a few days back, trying to sell a Nose Army radio. He swore he'd pulled it off an Army wagon sitting dead in the hills north-east of here.","
","^When the Farmers asked him where exactly, he filled his tank and left for Nose in a hurry. Now, I say a man that quick to leave has something to hide.","
","ev","str","^wagonBowl","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^You know the Glass Flats, out east, where the ground melted into glass? There's supposed to be an Old World tank out there that still runs. It rolls out at night with its lights off.","
","^My cousin saw it. Well, he heard it, and my cousin hears a great deal when he's been drinking.","
","ev","str","^glassTank","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"hattie_flats","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^Somebody every day, mind you. Traders, couriers, folk with a tank of fuel and a story to go with it. The ones that worry me are the quiet ones who ask where the seed stores are.","
","^Soldiers come down from Nose to buy water too. They're polite, I'll give them that.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"hattie_strangers","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^Soldiers playing at being a town, if you ask me. They eat our grain and send us orders back, and they're perfectly polite whenever they want something.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^Pim Arslan, who cuts lenses, says every ripple in it leans the same way, toward the Fallen Sun. That's the crater where the ship came down. My cousin says it points at heaven, but my cousin drinks.","
","^Sun or heaven, I won't stand on it at noon. The Sunward have their own opinion, mind. They worship whatever lies in that crater, and they'll share it with anyone who stands still.","
","ev","str","^talkGlassLean","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"hattie_sunward","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^That's what they say. A stranger goes into the crater with the Sunward and doesn't come out. I say folk do come out, green at the edges and quiet.","
","^I've never followed one in. Water's for paying folk, not for asking.","
","ev","str","^talkSunwardTake","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","end",null]}],null]}],"global decl":["ev","str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"depot_thief"},false,{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen"},"str","^off","/str",{"VAR=":"intro_step"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pipe_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"sack_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"lamps_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"count_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"courier_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"names_vosk"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"hooks_report"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_fate"},"str","^hidden","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_pact"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"bend_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"crates_fate"},false,{"VAR=":"hattie_flats"},false,{"VAR=":"hattie_sunward"},false,{"VAR=":"hattie_strangers"},"/ev","end",null]}],"listDefs":{}}

{"inkVersion":21,"root":[["
",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^Jory Baptiste. I speak for the tenants, which is to say I talk and the Senate nods off. Sit down, the stool's free. It's the only free thing in Bowl, so enjoy it.","
",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^Who are the tenants?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^How does a tenant get a vote?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^Why do you send tenants into the patrol?","/str",{"VAR?":"jory_patrol"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":5},"ev","str","^Does the patrol trouble you?","/str",{"VAR?":"jory_filled"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":5},"ev","str","^What do the raiders have to do with the grain?","/str",{"VAR?":"jory_filled"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^Who is Bo Lindqvist?","/str",{"VAR?":"jory_filled"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^Why do the top terraces stay green?","/str",{"VAR?":"jory_green"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":5},"ev","str","^What do you make of Nose?","/str",{"VAR?":"jory_nose"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-7","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-8","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^We grow the food, and the citizens eat it. You can tell us apart by the dirt under the nails. We work the families' terraces and keep a share of what we grow. We've no vote in the Senate, so the families decide what we plant and what we're paid.","
","^The top terraces, where the old families live, stay green even in a dry year. Nobody's explained that to me, and I wouldn't dare ask. A miracle's a miracle.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"jory_green","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"jory_nose","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^He serves in the Bowl road patrol for a decade. Then the Senate lets him drop a pebble in a jar. My grandfather died one season short, which was bad timing, but he always kept his own schedule.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"jory_patrol","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^Because the Senate wrote the rule and I read it back to them slowly. They said service earns a vote, so I send them the service. They let tenants carry rifles on the road and pay half the cost on grain runs, and nobody asked what a rifle in a tenant's hands might mean on voting day.","
","^The first tenant to sign the patrol roll was Bo Lindqvist, who drives for the Granary. The patrol knows my face by now, too. I've noticed the patrol and the raiders in the south get paid out of the same sacks, but that's a longer story. I've been told I'm a long story myself.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"jory_filled","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^It does, and it knows where I live. They searched my house at night once and said they were looking for a rifle. They found a spoon, and I told them to keep it because I've got more. A man should be known by somebody.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^Kiln Camp, the raiders in the south, gets a sack from the Granary for every armed truck that crosses their road. The patrol is paid out of the tenants' share of the same grain. We pay Kiln and we pay the patrol, and we pay both with the same grain.","
","^The sack leaves the store once and the Senate counts it twice. Odile Marsh, who keeps the Granary, chalks the count on the gate at night. Go and read it, and you'll see both lines are our grain. The Senate says it all adds up, and it does, the way a bucket with a hole adds up.","
","ev","str","^talkGranaryGate","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^A tenant who drives for the Granary, and gentle as a tired ox. Don't joke with him about the fight he had on the road. I joke about everything else, but I know where the edge is.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^Because, if the word's right, a pipe runs from the seep up to the top gardens. The seep's the little spring in the rock above the terraces. No meter's allowed to read that pipe, and if you say so in the market they'll send for a meter, so I say it only here.","
","^Have I seen the pipe? No. I've seen the kitchen gardens up there, and they're very green for a dry year. Either the pipe exists or those cabbages are saints.","
","ev","str","^talkSeepPipe","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","^They ration everyone and call it kindness. A fed man in a line is still a man in a line. Ask me again in a famine and I might change my mind, or I might not, because I'm a stubborn fellow when I'm hungry.","

",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^Sit a while, the shade is free. I am Ruben, and I keep the canal gates. That means I decide which fields drink first, so I'm used to being cursed by people who are only thirsty. What is on your mind?","
",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^What is this place?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Who runs Bowl?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^Where can I get water, or find work?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":4},"ev","str","^What did your grandmother tell you about the old days?","/str",{"VAR?":"ruben_old"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":5},"ev","str","^What is the Fallen Sun?","/str",{"VAR?":"ruben_sun"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^What is the Fallen Sun really?","/str","str","^fallen-sun","/str",{"x()":"found","exArgs":1},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^What do you know about the Green Pit feeder?","/str",{"VAR?":"ruben_water"},"str","^green-pit","/str",{"x()":"found","exArgs":1},"||","/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":5},"ev","str","^What are the tenants saying?","/str",{"VAR?":"ruben_senate"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-7","flg":5},"ev","str","^Why did the Senate refuse the loan from Pierce?","/str",{"VAR?":"ruben_senate"},"/ev",{"*":".^.c-8","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-9","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^Bowl is a farm built in terraces down the inside of a crater. The canals here still carry water, and water runs downhill, and so do people. Folk came for the canals and stayed for the seed.","
","^My grandmother kept these same gates before me. She liked to say that a town is only a field that learned to talk.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"ruben_old","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^The canal families do. Every gate has a family that tends it, and every family has a say in the Senate, the council of citizens that decides for all of Bowl. It is a slow way to decide anything, but nobody I know has starved waiting for a quick answer.","
","^The tenants who work the terraces for the families aren't citizens, so they have no seat. In the last drought, Pierce Corporation offered the Senate a long loan of grain. Pierce insures trucks and lends money, and the Senate argued over that loan for a whole season.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"ruben_senate","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^Water is Hattie's trade. She keeps the well house and sells a bucket to anyone with coin. Work is Dag's, because he rides with the Farmers and knows what hauls are waiting.","
","^I only open the gates. The water that goes through them belongs to the families, and it comes down a feeder channel from Green Pit, a village with a deep well.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"ruben_water","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^She said the whole basin was orchards in her time, from wall to wall, and the canals ran full in every season. Then the sky fell and the fruit went with it. She never could agree with herself on which came first.","
","^What fell is what people call the Fallen Sun.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"ruben_sun","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^People say it was a ship, bigger than all of Bowl. It came down burning and dug a crater out in the basin. Some say it brought the end of the world with it, but I say the end was already here. The ship only added one more bucket to a field that was flooded already.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^So you've stood in that crater, and you know more of it than I do. Nose calls the ship a warship, and Hattie at the well house calls it a seed ship that lost its way. I can only tell you that nothing grows near it, and of any place that is the worst thing I know how to say.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^In a dry year the Senate hung a meter on it and claimed a share for Bowl, as if the feeder had ever been ours to measure. That year the well at Green Pit dropped by a hand's width, and nobody asked the well what it thought.","
","^Wendell Ondra died at the sluice there, the little gate where the feeder lets its water in. His niece Agnes keeps the book at the Pump Station, and she writes down every drop.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","^They say they feed Bowl and have no say in it, and they're right. The families never wanted to tell a tenant what to think, only what to plant.","
","^Jory Baptiste speaks for them on the terraces. He is quick, and I like him, and I vote against him anyway.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-8":["
","^Because Pierce wanted the canal gates as surety. If a dry year came and we couldn't pay, Pierce would own the water, and the families would be tenants on their own terraces.","
","^My grandmother would have thrown the man in the canal. The Senate only argued with him for a season, which I suppose is how we throw people now.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-9":["
","end",null]}],null]}],"global decl":["ev","str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"depot_thief"},false,{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen"},"str","^off","/str",{"VAR=":"intro_step"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pipe_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"sack_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"lamps_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"count_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"courier_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"names_vosk"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"hooks_report"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_fate"},"str","^hidden","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_pact"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"bend_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"crates_fate"},false,{"VAR=":"ruben_old"},false,{"VAR=":"ruben_sun"},false,{"VAR=":"ruben_senate"},false,{"VAR=":"ruben_water"},"/ev","end",null]}],"listDefs":{}}

","^Something warm runs into your left eye and keeps running. A single high note fills your ears, and under it, far away, your engine ticks as it cools.","
","ev","str","^Wipe your eye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Keep it shut.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen","re":true},"^Your sleeve comes away dark and wet. You blink until the cracked glass in front of you stops sliding sideways.","
",{"->":"look"},null],"c-1":["
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen","re":true},"^Behind the lid the dark beats in time with your heart. When you finally open your good eye, the glass in front of you is a web of cracks.","
",{"->":"look"},null]}],null],"look":[["#","^checkpoint: look","/#","^Out past the hood, where the dust is settling, the other truck has stopped side on, far enough that you could not hit it with a thrown stone. ","#","^page","/#","
","^Its gun is still swung toward you on the mount, and a thin grey thread of smoke climbs from the muzzle and leans away with the wind. Behind it, a figure in goggles stands braced in the bed with both hands on the grips.","
","^Your hands lie in your lap and will not lift. You wonder, quite calmly, how long a body keeps in this heat, and whether anyone would think to look.","
","ev","str","^Hold the gunner's gaze.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Close your eyes and wait.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^You cannot see the eyes behind the goggles. You look anyway, because it is the last thing left that you can choose.","
",{"->":"mercy"},null],"c-1":["
","^You listen to the wind push sand across the hood and wait for the sound you will not hear.","
",{"->":"mercy"},null]}],null],"mercy":["^The sound does not come. ","#","^page","/#","
","^When you look again, the barrel has swung up and away and points at nothing in the empty sky. The gunner pushes the goggles onto their forehead, spits over the side and climbs down.","
","^They walk to your truck slowly, a rifle slung across the back, and do not even glance at the cab as they pass your window. You hear the bed creak under their weight and the tarp lift, and for a while you hear them sorting through what you carried.","
","^On the way back they stop by your door. A dented canteen lands on the seat beside you, half full, sloshing. Then boots on gravel, a door slamming, and an engine climbing away into the flat until the wind takes it. ","#","^page","/#","
","^You are alive. You hold onto that thought the way you would hold a rope, and it is enough to keep the canteen in your lap while the dark comes up around the edges of everything, soft and patient and in no hurry at all.","

","^Grain, from the Granary to wherever the Senate points me. I'm late with this load because a pin on my ring was loose. A pair of steel pins holds the ring to the bed, and I've seen what one pin does on a bend. So I check both at every stop, and I'll check yours too if you let me.","
","^Every crossing of Kiln Camp's road costs the Granary a sack, so I keep my load tight. A sack's cheaper than a truck, I tell myself. Odile Marsh, the steward, chalks every sack on the gate at night.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"driver_haul","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^Empty, once you're between the towns. Each town guards the road by its own walls, and Nose won't pay for a guard on the rest. Every truck's its own patrol, and I'd sleep better with somebody else on the road.","
","^The Old Army kept the whole road once, before my time. And I hear folk past the canyon do it differently, but I've only heard it.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"driver_road","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^Odile's counts, and I've watched her chalk them. One board holds the sacks we pay Kiln. The one beside it holds the tenants' share that pays for the patrol. She was a tenant herself, and some of us still call her a turncoat behind her back.","
","^She counts every sack twice, at night, and she doesn't blink.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^I trust them to act like Kiln. If you pay, they let you through. If you fight hard they often let you through anyway, and if you do neither they strip the truck down to the frame.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^Good drivers. They sit at the back of the hall and don't complain, and I've seen worse men with a vote.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^It ended and left hungry soldiers behind. My uncle was in it. He told me how soldiers came to the gate of Old Orchard, its depot, at night and were turned away. Some of them are on my crew, and I'll say this for hungry soldiers, they make fine drivers.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^The tale is that trucks there carry no guns, because a guard every town pays for keeps the roads. Lusa Fenwick rode west with a convoy once, and she came back telling it. She's a dreamer.","
","^I haven't been west, and neither has anyone who swears to it.","

facts.name: lamps_seen
facts.text: Posts: every lamp is painted with a Pierce lien number. Under the flaking paint on one post an older number shows, in a thinner hand.

facts.name: juno_said
facts.text: Juno: she sells oil to the Bowl first and lights the lamps with what is left. The last lamp is resting, she says.

facts.name: tam_said
facts.text: Tam: the oil can is lighter every week. The last lamp is dry, and a Pierce tag is wired to its post.

facts.name: slip_read
facts.text: Carter's slip: the Granary pays for the oil, and the coin goes to a Pierce clerk. Juno's name is not on it.

","^The cap is too hot to hold for long. Heat comes up off the bare rock in slow sheets, and the shirt on your back dried stiff with salt hours ago and has not been wet since.","
","ev","str","^Wipe your mouth.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Tuck the canteen away.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","ev","str","^walk","/str","/ev",{"VAR=":"intro_step","re":true},"^Your lips are split in the corners, and the back of your hand comes away gritty and faintly pink.","
",{"->":"rim"},null],"c-1":["
","ev","str","^walk","/str","/ev",{"VAR=":"intro_step","re":true},"^It knocks against your hip with every step, a hollow little sound that keeps you company whether you want it or not.","
",{"->":"rim"},null]}],null],"rim":[["#","^checkpoint: rim","/#","^The rock you have been climbing all morning ends at an edge, and beyond the edge the world drops away into a basin so wide that its far side is only a paler line in the haze. ","#","^page","/#","
","^Dust hangs over the flat like breath on cold glass. Far to the north a thin line runs through it that could be a road, and past that, too far to tell, the haze thickens around something that might be a town or might be nothing at all.","
","^Below you, at the very foot of the slope, a single water tower stands over a scatter of roofs. Nothing moves down there, and no smoke rises.","
","ev","str","^Look back the way you came.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Look down at the slope.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^Behind you there is only rock and the shimmer over it, the same as yesterday and the day before. Whatever you left back there, it is not coming after you.","
",{"->":"slope"},null],"c-1":["
","^It is loose scree most of the way, a long tilted field of it, then hard dirt, then the tower.","
",{"->":"slope"},null]}],null],"slope":[["#","^checkpoint: slope","/#","^You go down sideways, the way you would go down a roof, and the stones skate away from your boots and clatter on long after you have passed. ","#","^page","/#","
","^The sun settles on the back of your neck and stays there. For a while you sweat, and then you stop sweating, and you know that the second part is the bad part.","
","ev","str","^Rest in the shade of a boulder.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Keep walking.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^The shade is no thicker than paper. You sit in it anyway and count your breaths until they slow, and then you make yourself stand before sitting starts to feel like a good idea.","
",{"->":"farm"},null],"c-1":["
","^You do not stop. Some part of you understands that if you sit down now you may decide not to get up.","
",{"->":"farm"},null]}],null],"farm":[["#","^checkpoint: farm","/#","^Up close, the tower is taller than it looked from the rim, its tank rusted the color of dried blood and held up on legs so thin that you wonder why it has not walked off in the wind. ","#","^page ","/#","#","^place: The farm","/#","
","^Around it a farm has been given back to the dust. Fence posts lean at every angle but the one they were set at, the house has let its roof down onto its floor, and a loose sheet of tin knocks against something in a slow and patient rhythm.","
","ev","str","^Try the tap under the tower.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Call out.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^The handle gives with a shriek. The pipe coughs once, spits a thread of rust onto your boots, and gives nothing else, however long you hold it open.","
",{"->":"shed"},null],"c-1":["
","^Your voice goes out across the yard, cracked and smaller than you meant it, and nothing sends it back.","
",{"->":"shed"},null]}],null],"shed":[["#","^checkpoint: shed","/#","^Behind the tower stands what is left of a shed, a frame of grey boards that has folded in on itself like a tired animal lying down. ","#","^page","/#","
","^Under the fallen roof sheet, out of the sun, there is a pickup. It is an old one, older than anyone you have known, built back when trucks were made square and heavy and meant to outlive their owners. The nose is a flat grille with a pair of round lamps set into it like patient eyes, and the paint has gone from whatever color it once was to the dull bare primer of something the sun has had for many years.","
","^The tires are soft but whole. The bed is boxed in with welded plate, and a machine gun sits on a swivel behind the cab, its barrel wrapped in rag against the dust, its mount bolted down with a pair of heavy pins.","
","ev","str","^Pull the door open.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Wipe the windshield first.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^The hinge screams loud enough to send something small scrabbling out from under the bed. A breath of air rolls out of the cab, warm and close, but cooler than the yard.","
",{"->":"truck"},null],"c-1":["
","^Your palm leaves a clean arc in the dust. Behind it the bench seat is split and patched with tape, the dash is bare metal, and the key is still standing in the ignition.","
",{"->":"truck"},null]}],null],"truck":[["#","^checkpoint: truck","/#","^The bench seat is hot through your trousers and smells of engine oil, old rope and someone else's tobacco, and the key is in the ignition as if whoever owned this only stepped out for a moment and forgot to come back. ","#","^page","/#","
","^You twist it. The starter grinds, slows and quits.","
","^You twist it again. The engine catches for the length of a breath, shudders the whole cab, and dies.","
","^You wait, with your forehead resting on the hot rim of the wheel, and you twist it a third time. It coughs, misses, coughs again, and then it holds, settling into a rough and lopsided idle that rattles the mirror and the loose glass in the door. It is the best sound you have heard in days.","
","ev","str","^Ease out of the shed.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","ev","str","^drive","/str","/ev",{"VAR=":"intro_step","re":true},"^The roof sheet scrapes the length of the cab and slides off the tailgate behind you. Then the light hits the windshield, and the whole empty basin lies open in front of the hood.","
","end",null]}],null],"global decl":["ev","str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"depot_thief"},false,{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen"},"str","^off","/str",{"VAR=":"intro_step"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pipe_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"sack_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"lamps_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"count_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"courier_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"names_vosk"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"hooks_report"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_fate"},"str","^hidden","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_pact"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"bend_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"crates_fate"},"/ev","end",null]}],"listDefs":{}}

{"inkVersion":21,"root":[["#","^view: page","/#","
",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":[["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^Somewhere close by, a bucket is being drawn up a well on a creaking rope, and it takes you a long time to understand that it is the first sound in days that is not an engine or the wind. ","#","^place: Bowl","/#","
","^You are lying on a bench under a roof of woven reeds, with your cheek against wood worn smooth by many hands. Past the edge of the shade there are canals, real ones, full of slow brown water, and beyond them terraces of green so bright after the dust that it hurts to look at.","
","ev","str","^Sit up.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","ev","str","^done","/str","/ev",{"VAR=":"intro_step","re":true},"^The world tilts, considers you, and settles. Your pickup stands parked crooked at the edge of the yard with its hood propped open, and a tow chain that is not yours still hangs coiled from its bumper.","
","^The bed is empty. Someone has been through the engine bay in a hurry and left the bolts lying where they fell. Whoever brought you here did not stay to be thanked.","
",{"->":"hattie"},null]}],null],"hattie":[["^A broad woman with flour on her forearms sets a cup of water on the bench beside you, then sits down at the other end of it as if she has all afternoon and means to spend some of it on you. ","#","^page","/#","
","^Drink it slow, now. Fellow towed you in at first light, set you on my bench and drove off before I could get a word out of him. Didn't leave a name, and I didn't hear one. ","#","^speaker: Hattie","/#","
","^She looks across at the open hood and shakes her head the way people do at weather.","
","^The yard by the gate will sell you whatever they took, if you have the coin for it. You won't get far in that truck the way it is, and you won't get far in yourself either until you've had something to eat. ","#","^speaker: Hattie","/#","
","ev","str","^Drink.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^The water is cold and tastes of the canal stone, and you drink it so fast that it hurts your teeth. A bowl of hot grain follows it without being asked for, and then another cup.","
","end",null]}],null],"global decl":["ev","str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"depot_thief"},false,{"VAR=":"first_knockout_seen"},"str","^off","/str",{"VAR=":"intro_step"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pipe_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"sack_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"lamps_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"count_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"courier_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"names_vosk"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"hooks_report"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_fate"},"str","^hidden","/str",{"VAR=":"pin_pact"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"bend_fate"},"str","^none","/str",{"VAR=":"crates_fate"},"/ev","end",null]}],"listDefs":{}}

",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^Order Bureau, records. Keep your voice down, please. The corridor listens.","
",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^What does the Bureau do?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^What is wrong with the steel mounts?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_mounts"},{"VAR?":"asked_mounts"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":5},"ev","str","^What is in the account box?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_box"},{"VAR?":"asked_box"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":5},"ev","str","^Tell me about Emil Kessel.","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_kessel"},{"VAR?":"asked_kessel"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":5},"ev","str","^What case did she prove?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_case"},{"VAR?":"asked_case"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^What about the depot business?","/str",{"VAR?":"depot_thief"},"str","^none","/str","!=",{"VAR?":"depot_thief"},"str","^open","/str","!=","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^We keep files, and each file keeps a person. Please don't ask me whose. I sign for the steel mounts the line hands out with the gate passes. On market days I carry the Committee's account box to the Pierce office, where the insurers sit. Those are the errands I'm trusted with.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_box","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_mounts","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^Every one of them has a single pin. I signed for each one anyway. That's the part I think about at night. The first file I opened on the matter was the death of a driver named Emil Kessel.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_mounts","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_kessel","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^I don't know. It goes in heavy and comes back lighter. I don't open it, and I don't count what's inside. A clerk who counts is a clerk who gets asked questions later.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_box","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^I filed it. He was a driver on the north bend. His mount slid on its single pin and swung the gun into the cab. A captain signed the file, and nobody wrote a word about the pin. His sister is an inspector of this Bureau, Mara Kessel. She serves at the Army post inside the Salvage Yard now, and she doesn't come to this corridor. She once proved a case in these rooms. It's closed.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_kessel","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_case","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^I only say what the corridor says. A clerk at the Pierce office sold the roads of insured trucks to robbers. When it came out, he was sent west and told to stay. The Bureau had a case, and the case is closed. I carry the box that closed it.","
","ev","str","^talkClerkWest","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","

",{"->":".^.^.^.8"},null]}],["du","ev","str","^pell","/str","==","/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["pop","

",["done",{"#n":"g-0"}],null],"done",{"start":["#","^checkpoint: start","/#","^The Pierce office at Nose is a narrow room with a high desk and a locked cabinet. Constance Pierce does not stand when you enter.","
","ev",{"VAR?":"crates_fate"},"/ev",["du","ev","str","^proof","/str","==","/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["pop","
","^The board has the file. My cousin has not spoken to me since. That is a fair price. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":"start.12"},null]}],["du","ev","str","^lucan","/str","==","/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["pop","
","^My cousin has a new clerk he did not have last month. I wonder what the clerk is for. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":"start.12"},null]}],["du","ev","str","^buried","/str","==","/ev",{"->":".^.b","c":true},{"b":["pop","
","^You told me nothing. I will believe it until I do not. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":"start.12"},null]}],[{"->":".^.b"},{"b":["pop","
","^State your business. Pierce charges by the quarter hour. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","

",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^Who are you?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Why does Pierce insure only armed trucks?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^Why a second pin?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":4},"ev","str","^Why does every truck carry a gun?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":4},"ev","str","^Where did all the guns come from?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":4},"ev","str","^You look like someone with a problem.","/str",{"VAR?":"crates_fate"},"str","^none","/str","==","/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^Constance Pierce. Head underwriter at this office. Augustin Pierce was my great-grandfather, and I do not use his name as a key. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^An unarmed driver loses his load, and we pay. An armed driver keeps it, or at least makes it dear. I wrote the rule. It is arithmetic. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^A mount with a single pin can slide on a bend. The gun comes round into the cab, and we pay for a driver and a truck. Now we insure only a mount pinned twice. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
","^We write no paper on a Nose mount with one pin. Nose drivers pay the Salvage Yard to bore the second. That is not my doing, and I do not stop it. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^The Army left and nobody took its place. The rifles went loose, and the road went open. A policy needs a thing to insure, and an armed truck is one. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
","^I do not say it is a good world. I say it is the one that pays its debts. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^The Army's, mostly. The old Pierce yard held Army trucks against a debt. The guns left the yard. I read the books before I trust a story. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^I have a cousin, Lucan. He runs this company. The old yard stripped the Army's guns and crated them. Crates marked with a wheel went to a dealer at the crossroads. Crates marked with a hook went north. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
","^Scrapjaw has more rifles than the road should hold. I cannot prove who sent them. I will not ask a clerk to look, because clerks have cousins too. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
","^Find me a paper or a mark that a board will read. Do not say his name aloud. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",["ev","str","^I will look.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^Not my business.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","ev","str","^cratesAsk","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","^I never forget a favor. I do not forgive a debt either. Remember both. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
","ev","str","^crates_hook","/str",{"x()":"begin","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","end",null],"c-1":["
","^Then we have not spoken. ","#","^speaker: Constance","/#","
",{"->":"start.hub"},null]}],null],"c-6":["

facts.name: ledger_read
facts.text: Ledger: cans went missing on the third, seventh and eleventh nights. Pell was on duty each time.

facts.name: gate_checked
facts.text: Gate log: Corporal Vance signed out late on the third, seventh and eleventh nights, alone, with an empty truck bed.

facts.name: saw_swap
facts.text: Fuel shed: Vance asked Pell to swap shifts tonight. Pell agreed without looking up. Vance has a scar across his chin.

facts.name: knows_scar
facts.text: Sabine: a corporal brings her the cans. Big hands, a scar across the chin. Never a name.

facts.name: found_seals
facts.text: Barracks: a tin of Army fuel seals under Vance's cot, cut clean.

facts.name: saw_handoff
facts.text: Back fence: at dawn Vance passed cans over the wire to a truck with Sabine's mark.

","^Freeze, mostly, and listen. The Army pays me for its own calls, and whatever else drifts through I keep for myself. There's Jill Jane, who runs Waste Of Time Radio and comes in best after dark. There's the couriers of the Guild calling their rounds. And now and then there's a tone out of the big hull that nobody can explain. The set itself is Old World work, built back when there were masts on every hill. It's cold work, but it's quiet, and I never wanted better.","

","^Bigger than anyone here thinks. Bowl folk will tell you it was all orchards, and that's rubbish. There were highways, power lines, towns bigger than Nose and Bowl put together. ","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_oldworld","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_army","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_bowl","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^Good people, slow talkers. They'd hold a meeting to decide whether to hold a meeting. Still, their grain keeps us fed, so the Army minds its manners with them.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_bowl","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^Scavengers gab about the Burnt Convoy now and then, that row of burnt trucks out on the road. Picked clean, they say. Nothing left but ash and bent rims, and not worth the fuel to go and look.","
","ev","str","^burntConvoy","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_convoy","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^Nobody knows, but I'd wager she moves it. Her signal's strongest at night, and it drifts like the mast is on wheels. Don't tell the Sergeant I listen to her. He thinks this shack is for the Army alone.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_jj","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^Ines Abend, who reads it out front, says it counts the years since the fall. A tone's a tone, though. I've listened a long while and I hear a tone. If it counts, it counts without me.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_tone","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^They carry the mail between the towns. They run in pairs now, one to drive and one to hold the gun. I remember when they went out alone, before the Kiln riders got bold. Kiln's the raider camp in the south. Tamsin Roe's the odd one, with no gun at all. I hear her call-sign more than any other.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_couriers","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","^A whole convoy went up in one night. Some say raiders did it. Some say a fuel truck blew and took the rest with it. I heard the last calls on the air, and nobody said who started it.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_convoy","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-8":["
","^Hungry. Commander Lind nailed a book of every unpaid promise to the gate at Old Orchard, the Army's depot, and then he died in the motor pool. I heard his last calls on the air. He read the whole list. The machine tools stayed behind in the shed, and somebody's still paying for those.","
","^Some say the Army didn't run out of food. They say it was starved on purpose. I say a man who starts a rumor like that wants a seat in the hall.","
","ev","str","^talkArmyStarved","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_army","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_tools","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-9":["

","^A tone comes out of the central hull. It repeats a number, and the number grows by one each year. The tower has listened to it since my great-grandfather's day. We think it counts the years since the fall. This year's number hangs by the tower door, in my hand.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^We watched the sky from the Alpha Tower, to learn where the ship came from and whether more are coming. We were many once. Now there are few of us, scattered. I keep the tower door and read the count from there and from here. The old families of Nose keep asking me for it.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_families","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^A number kept in one head is a number kept from everyone. The Society voted on it, and I spoke first for reading it in the open. Teo wouldn't agree. He'd kept the count close since he was young. When the vote went against him, the Society cast him out.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_teo","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^Many of them have a grandmother who woke in a pod. They want to know how long they've been waiting. I tell them the number, and they nod. Some of them say a word in the old tongue.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_families","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^Teo took the tower when my great-grandfather died of burns. He read the plate when nobody else could. He read the count to me at the crater rim and told me to keep reading it after him. People call him the Apprentice now. I don't. He was never anyone's apprentice but the sky's. After the vote, the Sunward closed the rim to us. They're the people who keep it. I haven't stood there since.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_teo","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_rim","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^The Sunward shut it to us after the vote. Their Preacher says we count their god's patience. I'd call that fair, if I believed in the god. We read from the tower now, and from here. The glow doesn't mind. The Sunward chant a number of their own at the rim. I'd give a great deal to know where they found it.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_rim","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_chant","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^A number, and it's larger than this year's. I believe it's where the count stops. I don't know how they came to it. Someone must have read further than we have.","
","ev","str","^talkSunwardNumber","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","

","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_courier","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-11":["

","^I keep the Army's trucks running. Anybody else's too, if they bring them to my bench. Engines, plate, mounts, whatever breaks. I can tell what's wrong with a truck by the sound of it pulling in.","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["
","^Every part does one job and fails at another. Heavy plate stops rounds, but it eats your speed. A big gun eats your deck on top of that. So buy what the road needs, not what shines on the shelf. And if you've got a gun on a swivel, look at the pins first. The swivel's the ring that swings the gun across your bed.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_swivel","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["
","^The Salvage Yard, a way south of here. The crews strip whatever gets towed in, so parts go for next to nothing. You'll have to put up with the smell of burnt oil. For real plate you want the Fallen Sun, the big hull in the crater. I say that through my teeth.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_sun","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-3":["
","^Green Pit, out past the road. The water there runs clean and nobody guards it. Fill your cans if you're out that way.","
","ev","str","^greenPit","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
",{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^Because the copy they bolt on at the gate has one. I've seen what one does on a hard bend. The mount slides and the gun swings round into your own cab. Otto Brann made the first swivel, at Ridge Wrecks. He gave his a second pin. He was right, and I told command so. Nobody asks a mechanic. The Yard will bore you a second pin for a fee. Pay it.","
","ev","str","^talkOnePin","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_pins","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_brann","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-5":["
","^The ones with his mark, yes. He signs every weld. A weld you can read is a weld you can trust. I've even seen Kiln riders running captured ones on their own trucks. Good steel doesn't care who owns it.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_brann","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_kiln","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-6":["
","^They're raiders from the camp in the south, and I'd sooner not fix a truck they've stripped. But the old woman who keeps their furnace, Dagny Brask, melts captured guns into tools. I own a few. They're decent. Don't tell command I said so.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_kiln","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","^Best metal I ever put a torch to, and the worst place to fetch it. The brass call that hull a warship. I'd like them to show me one gun mount on it. There isn't one. It's cargo holds, all of it. And the glare off the glass around it will blind you by noon.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_sun","re":true},"ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_glare","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-8":["

facts.name: saw_cut
facts.text: North bend: Emil's wreck is bare. The ring under the gun was torched off at the base. The bolts still stand in the bed.

facts.name: yard_tally
facts.text: Yard tally: a Nose steel ring, torch cut, bought as scrap the week Emil died. Sold on to a Kiln hauler.

facts.name: otto_read

facts.name: saw_roster

facts.name: has_ring
facts.text: Kiln: the ring with the gate stamp and a single pin hole. Bought from a rider.

",{"->":".^.hub"},{"hub":[["#","^checkpoint: start.hub","/#","ev","str","^Who are the families of the Burnt Convoy?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-0","flg":4},"ev","str","^What do you sell here?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-1","flg":4},"ev","str","^What is the road like out here?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":4},"ev","str","^Who runs this yard?","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-3","flg":4},"ev","str","^Is the Burnt Convoy picked clean?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_picked"},"str","^burntConvoy","/str",{"x()":"has_note","exArgs":1},"||",{"VAR?":"asked_picked"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-4","flg":5},"ev","str","^What was the book you sold the Yard?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_book"},{"VAR?":"asked_book"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-5","flg":5},"ev","str","^What else do you hear about Pierce?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_pguns"},{"VAR?":"asked_pguns"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-6","flg":5},"ev","str","^Why do you never take the last water?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_water"},{"VAR?":"asked_water"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-7","flg":5},"ev","str","^Why do the Kiln riders leave you alone?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_kiln"},{"VAR?":"asked_kiln"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-8","flg":5},"ev","str","^Has a rider ever come to you with nothing?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_rider"},{"VAR?":"asked_rider"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-9","flg":5},"ev","str","^What do you make of the Army post?","/str",{"VAR?":"heard_post"},{"VAR?":"asked_post"},"!","&&","/ev",{"*":".^.c-10","flg":5},"ev","str","^Goodbye.","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-11","flg":4},{"c-0":["
","^People who live in the burnt trucks, where the road stopped. We're not a camp. A camp has a flag and a man who wants to be called sir. We're first to any wreck and last to leave it. That's all we are. Men on the air say there's nothing left in our trucks to pick. They're welcome to think so.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_picked","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-1":["

","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_book","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-2":["

","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"heard_post","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-4":["
","^No. We pick it every week and the road leaves more. Rust grows new things. Old Ibo, the radio man at Nose, says otherwise on the air, to men who wouldn't drive out there for a gift. Good. Let him.","

","^A debtor book. We stopped a Pierce office truck on the road and took it off the seat. Pierce lends to the towns and insures the trucks, so that's a big name to cross. What it says isn't for sale, and what the Yard does with it isn't my business. The crane office has a shut door now. A shut door is a loud thing.","
","ev","str","^talkCraneBook","/str",{"x()":"note","exArgs":1},"pop","/ev","

","^That Pierce sold the Old Army's guns north to Scrapjaw, then made every driver buy a gun to get paper. I hear it from a pair of drivers who each swear the other one lied. It's good business, if it's true. A man who sells the fire and the bucket never starves.","

","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_pguns","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-7":["
","^A man with no water is a body, and a body is trouble. Leave him his water and he's a fool who walks on. Fools talk less than bodies. Also, my mother would find out. She finds out everything.","
","ev",true,"/ev",{"VAR=":"asked_water","re":true},{"->":".^.^.^"},null],"c-8":["
","^We have a deal. Kiln has a man named Kaplan who knows a fair split. What the riders leave on the road is ours. What we find of their dead, we bury with their boots on.
